title: Noise
intro: All circuits are noisy. The art is knowing where the noise comes from, how it reaches the output, and how much power, area or bandwidth you must give up to reduce it. This chapter follows Razavi, Chapter 7.

items: Noise statistics and types: average power, PSD, correlation, SNR, the analysis procedure; resistor and MOSFET thermal noise, kT/C, gate resistance, flicker noise and its corner.
Representing noise: output noise, input-referred voltage and current sources, correlation, the short/open method.
Single-stage amplifiers: CS, CG, source follower and cascode, integrated noise and SNR.
Current mirrors and differential pairs: filtering the reference, the $\sqrt{2}$ penalty of a pair, load and tail noise.

blocks.text: Rules of thumb: maximise $g_m$ of devices that amplify, minimise $g_m$ of devices that only bias; make devices big for low 1/f noise; keep the bandwidth no wider than the signal; and expect every 3 dB of thermal noise to cost a doubling of power.
